activities.name: Travelling in the harmattan
activities.note: nothing closes; the harmattan blows during the dry season, and the trade-off is the dust

windows.reason: the wind blows especially in December, January and February: dust off the Sahara can severely limit visibility for several days, and humidity can drop below 15%
the harmattan, a dry and dusty wind off the Sahara, runs from the end of November to the middle of March

activities.name: Crépissage of the Great Mosque, Djenné
activities.note: a community festival when the whole town replasters its mud mosque

windows.reason: the mosque gets its new coat of mud every spring, in April, just before the rainy season

activities.name: Sanké mon collective fishing rite, San
activities.note: a UNESCO-listed rite marking the founding of San: fifteen hours of collective fishing, then a masked dance

windows.reason: held in June, on the second Thursday of the seventh lunar month, at the start of the rainy season

activities.name: Yaaral cattle crossing, Diafarabé
activities.note: the Peul herds' return across the inner Niger Delta, a UNESCO-listed festival

windows.reason: thousands of cattle are driven across the Diaka in late November; the Saturday is set each year by river level and pasture
